summary: Dettol sales at Shukla Medical Store have dropped. A Patanjali rep visits every week, their hand wash is cheaper, they give about 18% margin against our 12%, and they have put up a display stand. Ravi promised to install our display stand next week and took an order for 15 bottles of Dettol liquid and 10 hand wash.
score_reason: Ravi took an order, captured useful competitor and margin intel and addressed visibility, but he communicated no scheme, did not respond to the margin gap, did not discuss dues and kept the order to two Dettol SKUs.

needs.quote: हाँ, display से फ़र्क पड़ता है। पतंजलि ने अपना stand लगा दिया है।

coaching.tip: Great probing. You asked for the exact competitor margin, checked what customers ask for, and then asked what counter placement would change. That sequence surfaced the real problem and led naturally to the display-stand solution.
When the retailer told you 18% vs 12% margin, respond with the current Dettol scheme or a value argument such as loyal demand or faster rotation, instead of leaving the margin gap unanswered.
Before closing, check stock of the other Northwind SKUs and suggest a new SKU suited to a chemist. Also confirm pending dues or a payment date so the order is larger and the visit is complete.

debrief: रवि, शुक्ला मेडिकल स्टोर की विज़िट ठीक रही, डेटॉल लिक्विड पंद्रह बोतल और हैंड वॉश दस का ऑर्डर मिला। आपने पतंजलि का मार्जिन और उनके स्टैंड की जानकारी बहुत अच्छे सवालों से निकलवाई, और काउंटर डिस्प्ले वाला सवाल एकदम सही था। अगली बार अठारह बनाम बारह प्रतिशत मार्जिन की बात पर हमारी चालू स्कीम ज़रूर बताइए, और बकाया भुगतान की बात भी कीजिए। अगला कदम: अगले हफ्ते डिस्प्ले स्टैंड लगवाना मत भूलिए।
